evidence.label: mcp-python-archive-extract-unconfined (critical/medium)
evidence.detail: An archive is extracted without validating member paths. A tar or zip entry may name `../` or an absolute path and write outside the destination; Python's extractall has historically done exactly that.
evidence.excerpt:
with tarfile.open(tarball, "r:gz") as tar:
            tar.extractall(tmpdir)

        # Move binary

evidence.label: mcp-python-ssrf-nonliteral-url (medium/low)
evidence.detail: An outbound HTTP request is made to a URL that is not a literal. If any part of it is caller-supplied, the server can be steered at internal hosts — cloud metadata endpoints, admin ports, other tenants.

evidence.label: authentication_model
evidence.detail: stdio transport: the client launches the server as a subprocess, so the OS process boundary is the auth boundary — `03` §4 does not penalise absent auth here

evidence.label: transport_security
evidence.detail: declared transport: stdio — launched as a subprocess by the client, so the security boundary is the client process, not a network port (`03` §4)

evidence.label: secret_handling
